newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber off near limit, July OSB rises limit up.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber off near limit, July OSB rises limit up.

text.p: CME lumber and products contracts moved sharply in opposite directions with lumber futures down for a near limit loss of $9.90 per thousand board feet in July in a surge of liquidation while July Oriented Strand Board (OSB) posted a limit gain of $10.00 on rumors of a fire at a Canadian mill, traders said.
July lumber fell $9.90 to $373.60 per tbf with other months down $8.00 to $6.40. July OSB was up the $10.00 limit at $148.50 with September up $4.00 per 1,000 square ft.
Long liquidation in lumber reflected reports of continued weakness in cash lumber. Canfor mill closings in Canada are also now being viewed as bearish to futures, traders said.
Rumors of a fire at an OSB mill in Canada sparked the rally in OSB futures, traders said. However, no information was available about what mill or company was involved.
